theme: Controlling a fetch: predicate, fetch limit and batch size

terms.definition: A rule that filters objects, for example only the notes that are not done.
terms.example: Add an NSPredicate so we only load unread notes.

terms.definition: A cap on how many objects one fetch may return.
terms.example: Set a fetch limit of twenty for the first screen.
terms.code:
import CoreData
let r = NSFetchRequest<NSManagedObject>(
    entityName: "Note")
r.fetchLimit = 20
print(r.fetchLimit)

terms.definition: The number of objects loaded into memory at one time while you scroll through the results.
terms.example: A small batch size keeps memory low for long lists.
terms.code:
import CoreData
let r = NSFetchRequest<NSManagedObject>(
    entityName: "Note")
r.fetchBatchSize = 10
print(r.fetchBatchSize)

video.description:
Learn to explain how to filter and limit what Core Data loads: NSPredicate, Fetch Limit & Batch Size, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
NSPredicate - A rule that filters objects, for example only the notes that are not done.
Fetch Limit - A cap on how many objects one fetch may return.
Batch Size - The number of objects loaded into memory at one time while you scroll through the results.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain NSPredicate, Fetch Limit and Batch Size in English?

dialogue.title: Load less, load faster
dialogue.setting: Speeding up a slow notes list

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the notes list is slow. We load every note, even the done ones.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add an NSPredicate to the request. It filters the objects.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Now the NSPredicate skips the done notes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The first screen only shows twenty notes, though.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then set a fetch limit. In our code, `fetchLimit` is twenty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does a fetch limit also make scrolling smooth?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not exactly. For that, use a batch size.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I thought they were the same thing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. The fetch limit caps the total. The batch size controls how many load into memory at a time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So we use the NSPredicate, the limit and the batch size together.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Each one helps in a different way.

dialogue.code:
import CoreData
typealias Req = NSFetchRequest<NSManagedObject>
let r = Req(entityName: "Note")
r.predicate = NSPredicate(format: "done == NO")
r.fetchLimit = 20
r.fetchBatchSize = 10
